text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein and Netanyahu discuss situation in the Middle East and pushing forward the peace process. No tangible results from U.S.-Israeli summit.
- Lawyer for Jordanian soldier who shot seven Israeli girls calls for a public trial. Charge sheet to be ready after Moslem feast of Eid al-Adha (late April). Says soldier is not insane.
- Ministerial committee set up to look once more into pay bonuses of public sector employees.
- Leaders of eight pro-government parliamentary parties approve merger. Leadership of new party to be approved during an interim period.
- Jordan welcomes Saudi decision to stop charging extra for Jordanian vehicles filling up with diesel.
- Japan to offer Jordan assistance of $200 million for development projects in 1997/98.
- Chance of an informal meeting of parliamentary upper and lower houses to discuss government plans for elections.

- Customs department discloses violations in commissions charged by export promotion organisation. It says organisation charged between nine and 16 percent on goods imported under a Jordanian-Egyptian protocol.
- Government official denies reports that the United States suggested a number of countries in the region should form a military alliance. Says Jordan does not plan to join any such alliance.
- Israeli press reports say officials in charge of school trip to Baqoura, where seven Israeli girls were shot dead by Jordanian soldier, were partly to blame.
- King Hussein tells Netanyahu that Palestinians have offered all that they can.
- Merger of eight centrist parties is expected to challenge Islamic Action Front in forthcoming elections.
